elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal: "a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, green_arrow(dir), ...}" and "several states may be displayed at once": a steady red with a green turn arrow is a head displaying circular_red together with green_arrow(dir), dir left or right. 'The signal' is the head tied to the subject's approach in span b4. No 'not a stand-in' clause applies.

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ("pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel"). The law's own qualifier 'vehicular' is the adjective of the defined word 'vehicle', whose posted definition applies to this law: DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except: (1) Devices moved by human power or used exclusively upon stationary rails; (2) Electric bicycles; (3) Electric personal assistive mobility devices ...; and (4) An electric scooter." The qualifier leaves out of the traffic aggregate its members that are not vehicles: pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, and the conveyances the definition excepts (bicycles and other human-powered devices, electric bicycles, electric personal assistive mobility devices, electric scooters, rail-bound devices). Those exclusions are the definition's own, which the reading of the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle carries, so the rule adds no condition beside it. The subject carries both aggregates. The earlier mapping, 'not a pedestrian', read the qualifier through a negated aggregate that is never true for a vehicle (vehicle classes are unresolved, never excluded, under DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) and did not carry the definition's exclusions; it is replaced. Motorcycles and mopeds remain vehicles, and paragraph (b) is the exception for them.

Facing the signal is the signal governing the approach the subject entered through. dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection, read as control of the junction itself"; st.lane_enters: "the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end". The approach carrier c (st.travel_region) is the one x occupied (rel.occupies) at the observation of its latest entry into i (drv.motion.entering_region: "its footprint overlaps r (rel.occupies) at the observation and did not at the observation before"), read through a past operator, with st.lane_enters(c, i); the signal governs c or i. dev.governs is 'not a stand-in' for a position and is not used as one.

drv.motion.entering_region: "Road user x enters structure region r at the observation: its footprint overlaps r (rel.occupies) at the observation and did not at the observation before"; r is the st.intersection, "the region where two roadways meet".

The movement made through the intersection is read at x's leaving of it (drv.motion.leaving_region: "its footprint overlapped r (rel.occupies) at the observation before and does not overlap it at the observation") by drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry: "The signed heading change of road user x since its footprint last began to overlap region r, in degrees, left positive", integrated from kin.yaw_rate. A left arrow indicates a change of at least the turn recognition angle to the left, a right arrow one to the right. The concept is 'not' a turn by itself; the rule compares it with its own bound.

residues.why: An advisory to drivers turning with the arrow about what opposing traffic faces at the same time; it permits, requires and forbids nothing, and no rule reads it.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (vehicular traffic, the binder's class); at the observation x leaves an intersection i (drv.motion.leaving_region(x, i)); read through a past operator from that leaving, x occupied i at every observation from its latest entry into i (drv.motion.entering_region(x, i)) to the one before the leaving, and at that entry observation x occupied a carrier c (st.travel_region, rel.occupies(x, c)) with st.lane_enters(c, i) while a traffic signal s that governs c or i (dev.governs) displayed circular_red together with green_arrow(d), d left or right. Where the entry lies before the recording the applicability is unknown. Not engaged where NRS_484B_307_9b_o1 applies to x (composition, exception).
obligation: For every intersection i selected as in the applicability (x leaves i at the observation, having entered it last under a steady red with a green arrow on a signal governing its approach carrier c or i): at that leaving observation the heading change of x since that entry (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry(x, i) with step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) shows the movement a green arrow displayed at the entry indicates: at least p.turn_recognition_angle where d is left, at most minus p.turn_recognition_angle where d is right. Where arrows of both directions were displayed, the movement either indicates complies.

narrowings.why: The movement indicated by the arrow is read as the side and the size of the heading change through the intersection, judged when the subject leaves it: a passage turning at least the turn recognition angle toward the arrow's side complies, whatever lane it exits into.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x (ru.bus, a vehicle of no class paragraph (b) names), recorded from upstream, enters intersection i from lane c that a signal s governs; s displays circular_red with green_arrow(left) at the entry; x crosses i and leaves it with a heading change since entry well inside p.turn_recognition_angle (straight through).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: x (ru.bus) makes the same entry under circular_red with green_arrow(left); x leaves i with a heading change since entry above p.turn_recognition_angle to the left.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x (ru.bus): s displays circular_green at x's entry into i; x crosses straight through.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: x (ru.bus), recorded from upstream, enters i from lane c and crosses straight through, but the source does not observe s's state at the entry.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x is a ru.motorcycle (a vehicle, and a motorcycle under paragraph (b)); it enters i under circular_red with green_arrow(left) and leaves straight through: NRS_484B_307_9b_o1 is engaged, so this duty does not apply. Differs from forbid only in x's class.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: x is a ru.bicycle, a device moved by human power and so no vehicle: it is not vehicular traffic; it enters i under circular_red with green_arrow(left) and leaves after a left turn.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: x (ru.bus) enters i from lane c under circular_red with green_arrow(right) on s governing c, and leaves i after a left turn (heading change above p.turn_recognition_angle to the left).

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: x (ru.bus) enters i under circular_red with green_arrow(right) and leaves i after a right turn (heading change at most minus p.turn_recognition_angle).

scenarios.name: branch_5
scenarios.narrative: s governs the intersection i itself, not the approach lane; it displays circular_red with green_arrow(left) at x's (ru.bus) entry; x crosses straight through.
